failure_reason: Akamai Bot Manager blocks the entire argos.co.uk site (including the homepage) at tier (a) direct HTTP fetch (requests: 403 Access Denied; curl_cffi impersonate=chrome124: 403 Access Denied on both '/' and any '/browse/...' category page) and at tier (b) Playwright chromium (headless domcontentloaded, and headed with channel='chrome' + --disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled + webdriver-property spoof + mouse-movement warm-up on the homepage first - homepage itself returned HTTP 403 'Access Denied' in every configuration). Tier (c) Claude-in-Chrome (a real connected browser extension) initially got through and successfully rendered 16 category listing pages with live product-count headers, but partway through the session (after roughly 18 page loads) it too began returning Akamai's 'Access Denied' edgesuite error page on every further request, including previously-unvisited URLs - confirming a session/IP-level block rather than a per-URL cache. Per STEP1 rule 4, requesting the host was stopped at that point instead of chasing the block further. Only the static XML sitemap files (/robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /browse_sitemap.xml) remained reachable via tier (a) throughout and were used to build the complete category tree. As a result roughly a third of the qualifying rows carry a real rendered qty (obtained before the block) and the remaining two-thirds carry qty=null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag, tree-confirmed from the sitemap only.
notes: ACCESS: tier (a) direct requests/curl_cffi got 403 on '/' and all '/browse/*' pages (Akamai edgesuite Access Denied), but the static sitemap files were exempt and returned 200: /robots.txt (curl_cffi impersonate=chrome124), https://www.argos.co.uk/sitemap.xml (sitemap index), and https://www.argos.co.uk/browse_sitemap.xml (165KB, 1505 URLs, the full site category tree with clean /browse/<dept>/.../c:<id>/ slugs, no facet/query noise). robots.txt has no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web disallow (only generic '*'->/wishlist,/list/*, plus Googlebot/Bingbot rules), so tier (c) was permitted. tier (b) Playwright (headless, then headed real-Chrome-channel with stealth flags and homepage warm-up) still got 403 on the homepage itself, so it was abandoned. tier (c) Claude-in-Chrome (one connected local browser extension) worked initially - loaded and rendered 16 category pages with real product-count headers - then began returning a cached-looking but actually-fresh Access Denied response (different Akamai reference IDs) on every subsequent request including brand-new URLs, so it was stopped per the first-block rule rather than retried further. TREE: built entirely from browse_sitemap.xml filtered to the 307 URLs under /browse/home-and-furniture/ (the Home & Furniture department; the other 10 top-level departments - appliances, baby-and-nursery, clothing, garden-and-diy, gifts-and-occasions, health-and-beauty, jewellery-and-watches, sports-and-leisure, technology, toys - were scanned and excluded as out of scope for textile/storage). Category names in the rows are the exact slug-derived / breadcrumb-confirmed names (breadcrumb confirmed on all 16 pages successfully loaded via tier c; for the remaining nodes the name is the humanised sitemap slug, unverified against a live h1/breadcrumb because the page could not be loaded). QTY: for the 16 loaded pages, qty = the exact 'N products' header shown above the grid (e.g. '318 products' on Duvets). For every other qualifying node, qty=null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag per STEP1 rule 3 - no number was estimated, inferred, or copied from a sibling. EXCLUDED: Lighting (ceiling/floor/wall/desk/outdoor lights, bulbs) - out of scope. Kitchen & Dining/Kitchenware non-textile/non-storage items (cookware, tableware crockery/glassware/cutlery, dish racks, kitchen scales, kitchen bins, kitchen roll holders, mug trees excluded as LOW-value holders were instead kept as a LOW-confidence Storage row, water filter jugs, knives, starter sets) - out of scope except where explicitly a storage/organisation node. Furniture (all bedroom furniture including ottoman-and-storage-beds which is a bed not a storage box, all living-room furniture, dining-room furniture except the textile seat-pads, office desks/chairs, kids bedroom furniture, bathroom cabinets/wall-cabinets/shelves under 'bathroom-furniture' since the site does not label them Storage, kitchen-furniture placeholder node with no subcategories) - Furniture task, not this one. Decorative Home Accessories (artificial flowers/plants/trees, candle holders, candles, clocks, indoor pots and planters, mirrors of every type, ornaments, picture frames, vases, wall art and prints, most Christmas decorations - baubles, crackers, lights, table/room decorations, tree decorations, trees, wrapping, wreaths and garlands, outdoor Christmas decorations, tree-skirts-and-stands excluded as a mixed fabric-skirt/hardware-stand node with no reliable primary type, Christmas candles/home-fragrance/cookware/tableware) - out of scope; purely decorative even where technically able to hold something. Home fragrance (electric diffusers, reed diffusers, room spray) - out of scope. Bathroom fixtures/accessories with no storage or textile function (bathroom accessory sets, bathroom bins as waste bins not organisers, bathroom mirrors, bathroom scales, toilet brushes/roll-holders/seats, towel rails and rings as hardware) - excluded per textile.md SS9 and storage.md SS14/SS28. Hardware (blind-and-curtain-accessories, curtain-poles-and-tracks, coat-hooks-and-stands, kitchen roll holders, clothes hangers) - excluded per textile.md SS5 hardware rule and storage.md's container-not-accessory principle. Cleaning supplies (mops, dustpans/brushes, window cleaners, carpet sweepers, cleaning products) and laundry non-storage items (clothes airers, clothes steamers, irons, ironing boards, washing lines) - out of scope; laundry-accessories (a mixed pegs/bags/misc catch-all) excluded as genuinely ambiguous rather than forced into Storage. Pet supplies (entire department - cat/dog/fish/small-pet/wildlife products) - out of scope per textile.md SS18/storage.md SS31. Hot water bottles - excluded, primary product is a rubber/PVC bottle not a textile item even though sold in the Bedding node. Picnicware and picnic accessories (picnic-blankets-and-baskets) - excluded as a mixed textile/general-merchandise node outside the home-textile/home-storage scope, consistent with prior workers excluding garden picnic-ware as out of scope. Moving-house-packs-and-bubble-wrap - excluded (packing material, not a storage container product); cardboard-boxes from the same moving-house-supplies node was kept as a genuine storage-box product (MEDIUM). Lunch boxes and kids-room-decorations - excluded as neither textile nor storage per rules. No View-All/Collection/search/product-detail URLs were used anywhere in this file; all URLs are the exact /browse/.../c:<id>/ category listing URLs read from browse_sitemap.xml.
